data.hypothesis: The best prior valid configuration used 8,192-element tiles and reduced 512 partials directly in one final CTA for n=4,194,304 (6.94 µs reported); the 2,048-element-tile candidate reported 8.62 µs. This experiment holds the 256-thread, 8,192-element first stage constant and tests whether reducing more than 256 partials in a separate grouping kernel—512 to 2 at the target size—offsets the additional launch. Smaller partial counts retain the two-stage path. No speedup is assumed before measurement.

memory_lessons.applicability: Comparison points for this reduction objective; the measurements do not isolate tile size as the sole cause.
memory_lessons.claim: Two prior candidates were correct on all ten supplied cases. The candidate described with 8,192-element tiles reported 6.94 µs mean, compared with 8.62 µs for the 2,048-element-tile candidate; these are measured configurations, not proof that tile size alone caused the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this additional-final-stage variant with the same correctness checks and repeated timing protocol.

data.notes: The extra grouping stage is used only above 256 first-stage partials. Scratch writes are bounded: at most 2,048 first-stage integers and at most 8 grouped integers, with the grouped region beginning after the first bank. The controller must establish correctness and performance; no candidate timings are available yet.
transformations: Replace modulo-based shared-memory reduction with per-thread accumulation across coalesced 8,192-element tiles using 256-thread blocks.
Use warp shuffles and one inter-warp shared-memory synchronization to reduce each block's values.
Cap first-stage partials at 2,048. Reduce up to 256 partials directly to output; otherwise group partials in a second kernel and reduce the grouped values to output in a third kernel.
Keep a one-block path for inputs up to one tile, a device-to-device copy for n=1, and a zero-output fallback for n<=0; bound and guard input reads.
